themes_summary: METHOD AND LIMITS: Bing returned off-topic results (Windows help, speedtest) for every Hebrew query, and DuckDuckGo served a bot challenge, which was not attempted. kolzchut.org.il and prog.co.il returned HTTP 403, and several tapuz.co.il threads returned errors. Mining therefore relied on WebSearch plus direct fetches. Real parent-forum phrasing came from tapuz, beofen-tv, infomed, doctors, inn.co.il, a mako parent Q&A (2011) and a parents' webinar (shavvim, 2026). Many of the 59 questions are FAQ headings on Israeli clinic sites, which mirror what parents ask clinics. Most forum threads are old (2004–2015).

WHO IT SUITS / READINESS (most common question): almost every competitor FAQ opens with 'is it right for my child?' Typical answers: suited to children who can benefit from a guided peer setting. Very high anxiety, severe dysregulation or trauma may need individual therapy first (https://www.rimonclinic.com/grouptherapysocial/, https://www.hevruta-center.com/faq-hevruta, https://thespectrum.co.il/content/%D7%98%D7%99%D7%A4%D7%95%D7%9C-%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%AA%D7%99/). Several groups are marketed specifically for children diagnosed HFASD and in mainstream education (https://www.overtherainbowcenter.com/qna, https://www.be106.net/233/162215).

AGE / WHEN TO START: competitors say groups can start in kindergarten. noamsystems says around ages 3–4. BSK runs groups for ages 3–4.5 and 4.5–6 (kindergarten), plus grades 1–6. Rehovot runs kindergarten–grade 1 and grades 2–6 (https://noamsystems.co.il/2025/03/11/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%A2%D7%9C-%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%A6%D7%A3-%D7%94%D7%90%D7%95%D7%98%D7%99%D7%A1%D7%98/, https://www.bsk.co.il/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%90%D7%95%D7%98%D7%99%D7%A1%D7%98%D7%99%D7%9D, https://www.be106.net/233/162215). Preparing for first grade is its own concern (https://oti.org.il/1st-grade-adjustment/). Galila's split of a kindergarten group and a grades 1–3 group matches how the market is organised.

GROUP STRUCTURE (size, duration, age gap): sizes quoted are 3–6 (thespectrum), 4–6 (d-ligdol), 4–5 (Rehovot), 3–5 (tipulpsychology), and up to 12 (smilemichal). Programmes run 10, 12, 14 or 20 sessions of 45–60 minutes, weekly. One clinic caps the gap at two school years (https://www.tipulpsychology.co.il/therapy/children/%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%91%D7%91%D7%99%D7%AA-%D7%A1%D7%A4%D7%A8.html), and a 2013 forum reply said groups struggle with a 2–3 year gap (https://www.tapuz.co.il/threads/%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%AA%D7%AA-%D7%AA%D7%A7%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%AA.13782928/). Parents also worry whether a group of only spectrum children leads to imitating unwanted behaviours (https://www.mako.co.il/home-family-kids/education/Article-76989722c6b7e21006.htm).

WHAT HAPPENS IN A SESSION / METHOD: parents ask what is actually done in a session, who leads it and what method it uses. Answers mention play, role-play, joining a game, reading social cues, emotional regulation, conflict resolution, 'social thinking' (Michelle Garcia Winner), PEERS, PPSI/PRT and CBT. The two-facilitator model is often highlighted (https://www.overtherainbowcenter.com/qna, https://haverim.me/%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%9C%D7%95%D7%AA/, https://nhn.co.il/kbvtzvt-myvmnvyvt-chbrtyvt-children-vbny-youth/). A ynet explainer by a group facilitator stresses imitation and the role of peers for children on the spectrum (https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5146865,00.html). No competitor found explicitly combines ABA, CBT and paramedical professionals the way Galila does, which is a differentiator.

GROUP vs INDIVIDUAL THERAPY vs AFTER-SCHOOL CLUB: frequent FAQ topics include 'is a group better than individual therapy?', 'can we do both at the same time?' and 'what is the difference between a therapy group and a social club (חוג חברתי)?' (https://haverim.me/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%AA-%D7%9E%D7%99%D7%95%D7%9E%D7%A0%D7%95%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA/, https://www.rimonclinic.com/grouptherapysocial/).

COST AND FUNDING (parents ask often, few sites answer): Haverim (Tel Aviv) charges ₪500 for the intake and ₪390 per session, with at least 20 sessions (https://haverim.me/%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%9C%D7%95%D7%AA/). Rehovot (Havayot) charges ₪150 per session for 12 sessions (https://www.be106.net/233/162215). A Tel Aviv CBT group package costs ₪4,820 (https://www.tipulpsychology.co.il/therapy/children/%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%A9%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%91%D7%91%D7%99%D7%AA-%D7%A1%D7%A4%D7%A8.html). A Haifa University teen group (ages 14–16) costs ₪200 per session according to a search snippet, not fetched (https://icc.haifa.ac.il/2026/01/18/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%94-%D7%9C%D7%A4%D7%99%D7%AA%D7%95%D7%97-%D7%9E%D7%99%D7%95%D7%9E%D7%A0%D7%95%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%9E%D7%AA%D7%91%D7%92/).

HEALTH FUNDS: Maccabi's basic basket for children with an ASD diagnosis up to age 17 covers up to 3 sessions a week (156 a year) of speech, OT, physio, social work or psychology. Co-pay is ₪37.70 from age 3. Children in a communication kindergarten with TAM are excluded. Reimbursement for private therapists is being phased out from 1.2.2026, and the page does not mention group therapy (https://www.maccabi4u.co.il/eligibilites/2733/?id=1527). Leumit likewise offers up to 3 sessions a week until age 18 (https://www.leumit.co.il/child-development/the-autism-spectrum-in-children-identification-diagnosis-and-treatment/). BSK says HMOs or private insurers 'may reimburse' its groups (https://www.bsk.co.il/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%90%D7%95%D7%98%D7%99%D7%A1%D7%98%D7%99%D7%9D). Reimbursement for social groups specifically is unclear, which makes a careful answer a content opportunity.

SCHOOL ROUTE: per the Ministry of Education, a student on the spectrum in individual integration is entitled to a programme that includes 'קבוצה חברתית ושעות סיוע' (https://parents.education.gov.il/prhnet/special-education/disabilities-types/autism/autism-assistance-education-systems). A ynet article notes that schools sometimes run a small group with 2–3 classmates the child chooses (https://www.ynet.co.il/health/article/hkh34bmjgg). Parents weigh communication kindergarten against a regular kindergarten with an aide, speech-support teacher or personal support package (https://www.tapuz.co.il/threads/%D7%90%D7%95%D7%98%D7%99%D7%96%D7%9D-asd.14527218/, https://www.inn.co.il/forum/t1133214).

'MY CHILD HAS NO FRIENDS' / RECESS: this is the biggest emotional entry point and recurs across ynet, mako, kikar and hidabroot headlines ('אין לי חברים', 'לבד בהפסקה', 'אף אחד לא רוצה לשחק איתו'). A psychiatrist calls the belief that children on the spectrum don't want friends 'a mistake', says withdrawal can be self-protection after repeated rejection, and names recess as the hardest part of the day (https://www.ynet.co.il/health/article/hkh34bmjgg). One clinic FAQ addresses 'he says he doesn't care about friends' directly (https://www.hevruta-center.com/faq-hevruta).

FEARS AND RESISTANCE: parents worry the child is too shy, will refuse to go, or will suffer the same hurt in the group as in class. Clinics answer with gradual entry, starting as an observer, and two facilitators (https://smilemichal.co.il/service/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%98%D7%99%D7%A4%D7%95%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA/, https://noamsystems.co.il/2025/03/11/%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9D-%D7%A2%D7%9C-%D7%94%D7%A8%D7%A6%D7%A3-%D7%94%D7%90%D7%95%D7%98%D7%99%D7%A1%D7%98/, https://haverim.me/%D7%A9%D7%90%D7%9C%D7%95%D7%AA/).

PARENTS' ROLE: parents ask whether they are involved, how to support at home, and what parent guidance is. Models include a monthly parent meeting (d-ligdol, Haverim). Oti cites the Ministry of Health view that parent guidance counts as 'direct treatment of the child through the parents' (https://oti.org.il/parenting-guidance/). Galila's parent-guidance component addresses this directly.

DIAGNOSIS LANGUAGE: parents ask whether it is autism or just poor social skills or social anxiety, what 'high functioning' or levels 1–3 mean, and Asperger vs ASD. Asperger has not been a separate diagnosis since DSM-5 in 2013, but parents still search for it (https://www.tipulpsychology.co.il/therapy/children/asperger-s-disorder.html, https://www.tasmc.org.il/bewell/interestareas/default/autism-or-social-anxiety/, https://www.mako.co.il/home-family-kids/education/Article-76989722c6b7e21006.htm).

SIBLINGS AND FAMILY: parents ask how to tell siblings, cousins and grandparents, and siblings ask 'why am I autistic and you're not?' (https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5488257,00.html, https://shavvim.co.il/2026/05/04/%D7%9E%D7%94%D7%95-%D7%90%D7%95%D7%98%D7%99%D7%96%D7%9D-%D7%91%D7%AA%D7%A4%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%93-%D7%92%D7%91%D7%95%D7%94-%D7%95%D7%9B%D7%99%D7%A6%D7%93-%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%AA%D7%9F-%D7%9C%D7%94%D7%AA/, https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5287197,00.html). Disclosing the diagnosis to the child is a separate recurring question.

LOCAL / SEO NOTE: for 'קבוצה חברתית לילדים על הרצף חיפה', WebSearch surfaced Galila's own Facebook page (https://www.facebook.com/p/%D7%92%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%9C%D7%94-%D7%A7%D7%91%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%94-%D7%97%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%AA-100088575528100/), not galilagroup.com. Other Haifa results were a teen group (14–16) at Haifa University and a general CBT clinic, with no dedicated ages 4–9 spectrum competitor visible. Tel Aviv competition is denser: Haverim, d-ligdol (grades 3–6), Efsharuyot (pre-first-grade, Ramat HaHayal) and tipulpsychology (ages 8–12). Most competitor pages state no price, few answer reimbursement clearly, and none target ages 4–9 with an ABA+CBT team. A FAQ section on galilagroup.com answering the questions above (with schema.org FAQPage) would fill a visible gap.

funding.summary:
How Israeli parents fund therapy for children with ASD (checked 22.10.2026). The direct public sources were the Kol Zchut pages, Clalit, Maccabi, Meuhedet, Leumit, the btl.gov.il rates page, the Tel Aviv municipality site, and Bing autosuggest (he-IL). DuckDuckGo HTML returned a CAPTCHA, which I did not solve. gov.il and call.gov.il pages were blocked (403) or rendered empty, so the one gov.il figure comes from a search-engine excerpt and is marked medium confidence.

1) Basic health basket (סל הבריאות). It funds up to 3 paramedical treatments a week (156 a year at Clalit, Maccabi and Leumit) from diagnosis to age 18. The professions are speech therapy (קלינאות תקשורת), occupational therapy (ריפוי בעיסוק), physiotherapy, psychology and social work. There is a co-pay from age 3. Children under 7 who get TABAM (טב"ם, a Ministry of Health package in designated frameworks) are excluded. None of the fund pages reviewed lists a "קבוצה חברתית" or social-skills group as a named basket service. Maccabi's autism page does not mention group treatment at all.

2) The reform is the most important change for private providers. It started 1.2.2026, and the funds are phasing out reimbursement for private child-development treatments:
- New patients under 6 with autism lose reimbursement from 1.1.2027.
- New patients aged 6–18 with autism lose it from 1.1.2028.
- All reimbursements end 1.1.2030.
- Since 1.12.2025, Maccabi only reimburses private therapists who hold a Ministry of Health licence (speech, occupational or physiotherapy) or are registered social workers, and have at least 4 years in public developmental institutions.
- Leumit says the change does not apply to supplementary insurance (ביטוח משלים) entitlements.

3) Supplementary insurance (ביטוח משלים, also called שב"ן) is the realistic path for art therapy (הבעה ויצירה), and only through providers that have an arrangement with the fund (ספקים בהסדר):
- Clalit Mushlam: emotional treatments for ages 3–18, including arts therapy, up to 30 a year in Zahav. Arrangement providers only, 6-month waiting period.
- Maccabi Zahav/Sheli: complementary treatments for children with ASD aged 3–17, including expressive and creative therapy. 45 ₪ per treatment, up to 30 + 20 a year.
- Maccabi psychotherapy with therapists in agreement: group therapy costs 78 ₪ per session.
- Meuhedet Si: 40 emotional treatments a year up to age 12.
- Leumit: lists group therapeutic sport and art therapy among emotional treatments for children with ASD. Leumit Zahav covers 55 child-development treatments a year.

4) Bituach Leumi disabled-child allowance (גמלת ילד נכה). An autism diagnosis entitles the child to the 100% rate: 3,820 ₪ a month in 2026, and 7,181 or 9,126 ₪ when the child is fully dependent on others. Bituach Leumi describes it as sharing the family's costs of raising the child, with no restriction on how it is used. No source quantified how parents spend it. Related benefits:
- Exemption from health-fund co-pays for specialists, outpatient clinics and diagnostic institutes.
- 2 income-tax credit points (5,808 ₪ a year).

5) Welfare and municipal support. It requires recognition by the Welfare Ministry, arranged through the local social-services department. Recognized children can get:
- An afternoon club (מועדונית) with individual and group treatment for social skills, or alternatively a mentor (סומך). Both carry a co-pay.
- Camp subsidies for children in regular education.
- Tel Aviv also refers families to children's clubs and mentors, and runs the "תותים" centre.
- Separately, the national "רעים" programme at community centres (מתנ"סים) runs weekly social groups with a co-pay.
- There is no single autism fund (no "סל אוטיזם"). In practice the term means the health-fund autism basket: Clalit's "סל טיפולים לילדים עם אוטיזם", which appears in autosuggest as "סל אוטיזם כללית".

6) What people search for (Bing he-IL autosuggest):
- Parents pair "טיפול רגשי לילדים" with fund names (כללית, מכבי, מאוחדת, כללית מושלם) and with חיפה.
- "הדרכת הורים" with "לילדים על הרצף", מכבי or כללית מושלם.
- "ביטוח לאומי" with "ילד נכה אוטיזם" or "הגשה".
- "קבוצה חברתית" with "תל אביב מוגבלות".
- "כללית מושלם" with "טיפול באומנות" or "החזר".
- Long phrasings such as "קבוצה חברתית לילדים על הרצף" or "החזר טיפולים אוטיזם" returned no suggestions.

What this means for Galila: content that explains funding (basket vs. supplementary insurance, the 2027–2030 changes, the disabled-child allowance, Welfare Ministry recognition) matches real searches. But no public source here confirms that a private social-skills group is covered. Galila would need to check directly with each fund whether it can join as an arrangement provider (for art therapy, or for group psychotherapy at Maccabi).

claims.claim: ילדים שאובחנו על רצף האוטיזם זכאים לטיפולים פרא-רפואיים מקופות החולים (ריפוי בעיסוק, פיזיותרפיה, קלינאות תקשורת, פסיכולוג או עובד סוציאלי), עד 3 טיפולים בשבוע לאורך כל השנה, מגיל האבחון עד גיל 18.

votes.reason:
The numbers in the claim are correct. Its blanket wording ("children diagnosed with autism are entitled") is wrong for one group, though, and that group overlaps the site's own audience of ages 4–9. So I am marking it refuted on the "missing a condition" ground and giving a corrected wording below.

WHAT CHECKS OUT
1. The cited source supports the claim almost word for word. The Kol Zchut page (https://www.kolzchut.org.il/he/טיפולים_פרא_רפואיים_לילדים_אוטיסטים, last updated 2 March 2025) says:
   - the therapies are occupational therapy, physiotherapy, speech therapy, and treatment by a psychologist or social worker;
   - the entitlement is "up to 3 treatments a week, all year round";
   - it applies "from the age of diagnosis until age 18".
2. The Ministry of Health page (https://me.health.gov.il/mental-health/information-and-updates/autism/entitlements-for-children/, updated 6 October 2026) confirms up to 3 paramedical sessions a week in the same five professions. It also says a formal autism diagnosis is required.
3. Clalit (https://www.clalit.co.il/he/myrights/autism-spectrum-disorder/Pages/asd-treatments.aspx, updated 1 February 2026) confirms ages up to the 18th birthday and up to 3 treatments a week.
4. Maccabi (https://www.maccabi4u.co.il/eligibilites/2733/, updated 25 August 2026) confirms up to 3 treatments a week up to age 17 inclusive, which is the same as up to 18.
5. Leumit (https://www.leumit.co.il/en/child-development/rights-of-children-with-autism/) confirms ages up to 18 and the same professions. It gives no weekly number.

WHAT THE CLAIM LEAVES OUT
1. An exclusion group. Children up to age 7 who receive "health-promoting treatment" (טיפול בריאותי מקדם, the ministry-funded therapy package given inside dedicated autism settings) are not entitled to these treatments from the health fund.
   - Kol Zchut lists this group under "Who is not eligible?".
   - Clalit says these children "will not receive the treatments from the health funds, even if the package they receive is incomplete". It applies this to children up to 7 in dedicated autism settings.
   - Maccabi says a child in a rehabilitative day-care centre or a communication kindergarten that gives this package "is not entitled to the treatments given in the basket".
   - This matters for the site: many children aged 4–7 attend communication kindergartens that provide this package.
2. "Up to 3" is a maximum, not a set number. Clalit says its authorised professional body decides the number together with the therapist.
3. There is a yearly cap of 156 treatments per calendar year (Clalit, Maccabi). "All year round" is correct in the sense that there is no summer break.
4. From age 3 there is a co-payment for each treatment, unless the family receives income support (Kol Zchut, Clalit). Maccabi lists 37.70 ILS per treatment at its own child development centres.
5. Treatment is arranged through child development centres (Kol Zchut).

One possible inconsistency: an older 2023 Knesset research document reportedly describes the 3 sessions as "3 hours". Current official sources say "3 treatments/sessions", so the claim's wording is fine.

Search engines (Bing, DuckDuckGo) and gov.il pages blocked automated access, so I could not open the full Ministry of Health circulars. The findings above rest on the Ministry of Health portal and the health funds' own pages.

Bituach Leumi's rates page states that from 01.01.2026 the disabled-child benefit is calculated as a percentage of a full single allowance of 3,820 ₪, with 100% = 3,820 ₪, 188% = 7,181 ₪ and 235% = 9,126 ₪ per month.

Bituach Leumi describes the disabled-child benefit as recognising the heavy care burden of raising a child with a severe impairment. It contributes to the family's financial expenses to ease raising the child at home and in the community. The page sets no restriction on how the money is spent.

For children diagnosed with autism after age 3, disabled-child benefit eligibility is set until age 18 and 3 months based on the diagnosis, without the child attending the medical committee. Children are summoned only if the committee doctor sees a need.
Recipients of the disabled-child benefit are automatically exempt from health-fund co-payments for secondary (specialist) doctors, hospital outpatient clinics, and imaging/diagnostic institutes.
הורים לילד המקבל גמלת ילד נכה זכאים ל-2 נקודות זיכוי ממס הכנסה, בשווי 5,808 ₪ לשנה (484 ₪ לחודש).

To receive community services from the Welfare Ministry, a child with ASD needs Welfare Ministry recognition, requested through the local social services department and decided by a 'trust psychologist'. Since 01.02.2019 recognition of a child is valid until age 18.

ילדים על הרצף שהוכרו על-ידי משרד הרווחה ומתגוררים בבית הוריהם זכאים למועדונית אחה"צ – מסגרת חינוכית טיפולית שניתן לקבל בה טיפול אישי וקבוצתי לשיפור מיומנויות חברתיות; יש לבחור בין מועדונית לשעות סומך.
Welfare-recognised children with autism aged 3+ living at home may get funding for a personal mentor (סומך) for some afternoon hours, with a co-payment based on family income.

Welfare-recognised children with autism in regular education can get help funding municipal summer camps, or camps that won a Welfare Ministry tender. Parents pay in full and claim a refund with the receipt at the local social services department.

- Few competitors target ASD ages 4 to 9 with a behavior analyst plus art therapist team.
